content.label: This is the perfect app for happily tracking the habits you need to do to stay healthy and happy. No distracting fluff but enough options to customize each habit to make it appealing to remember and to complete. Reminders are great as well. Super happy with it, and even better — it helps me hit my goals! So glad this app exists.

I love the set up, if you like the green squares of GitHub, this habit tracker is for you. However, I think it would be amazing if they implemented a folder or categorization feature. I want my career growth habits to be separate from my health and wellness habits.
HabitKit is a bit misleading, as you’d think ‘kit’ would imply some possible integrations. I would love to tap an NFC tag and log a habit.

This app is great for visualizing and tracking your habits in a multitude of different ways. I really like and value the customization aspect as well, and being able to see my growth never fails to boost my mood!
However, desperately needs an account and sync function because habits do not sync across devices.
This app is very simple and easy to use, but so versatile!

title.label: Great, simple, wish it had a note taking section for each habit

content.label: Note taking section would help better refine the habit and track triggers that set you off the track. I’d be willing to subscribe to pro for that.
Great app but desperately needs iCloud syncing.

Really great, functional app with beautiful widgets. Does its job in an easy to use, visually pleasing way on my phone. 

Once it gets an iPad app and iCloud syncing, which the dev says is on the roadmap, it’ll be a 5-star app!

title.label: The only habit tracker that makes me feel good!

content.label: I have tried many habit trackers but this is the only one that doesn't give me so much anxiety and stress when I miss my streaks. A lot of the other ones try to hold you accountable and stick to goals. While I do wanna do that, some days just make it hard and my busy schedule makes it hard to keep up with everything. HabitKit on the other hand lets you actually just keep tabs on your progress. Yes, maybe you missed a day or week, but you can always see your previous progress and remind yourself that you can still make it up and catch up! It's no surprise that other apps are copying this now! Sebastian's also a really responsive and friendly founder! Really happy to get to support this project!
I have been using this app for a while and I found it very useful. It’s super intuitive to use and having widgets is great.
I really like this habit tracker. Looking forward to updates and new features
Should make a Mac app and give unlimited habits for free. Other paywalled stuff is fine but leaves functionality for free users

This is the easiest and most intuitive habit tracker I’ve used and I’ve tried so many of them! It also works great with the shortcuts app so you can use an nfc tag or ask Siri to mark a habit for you!
Love it. Compared to very cluttered competitor apps, the UI’s simplicity and neatness is a breath of fresh air.  And it has all the functionality I was looking for

I use this app to review weekly smart goals. It’s perfect and does the job of tracking and presenting attractive reports quite well.  It’s not ideal for project management or to do lists, but does habits better than any other of the 20 apps I auditioned. I got the paid version and feel it’s worth it.

Nearly perfect…Would gladly pay for pro or lifetime if it meant I could choose custom colors for habits. As I use widgets to help me stay on track, I need an app that will fit with the color scheme of my background. Unfortunately this is not that app.
I’ve tested a lot of tracker and this one offers the best UX and visualization while keeping it simple and intuitive to use.

UPDATE (2025-02-05)

Not sure how long I’ve been using HabitKit (just checked and it has been a bit over two years) and I’m still loving it ♥️

It’s simple, has the features I want, and zero bloat. I love that you can enable/disable streaks because I’m no longer doing streaked habits.

I’ve been using it as a widget stack on my Home Screen (small size, all habits in the stack) and it’s just perfect like this!

—=•=— 

I’ve been using the “don’t break the chain” method of habit building for about a billion years. I’ve used apps and my own paper trackers. They all work, more or less, but some just feel better than others, and with something simple like habit tracking, feel is 90% of what’s important.

HabitKit has FEEL son!

There’s something about the simplicity of the app and the ease of logging that just feels right. But more than that, the visual display of your streak is the best I’ve come across. It’s RIGHT in your face. There’s no ignoring it… and that’s a very very good thing.
I feel like other apps overcomplicate routines and habits but this one is pleasant to use.

title.label: Pretty good except for the ads

content.label: It’s great but there are wayyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyy too many ads of premium

Overall this is the best habit tracker i found and i went thought a lot. It helps so much to visualize your habit consistency which not many other apps have. This app also does not come with the extra un needed fluff but one thing i would like to see is an option to mark that I did not complete one of my tasks that day such as a red dot. Overall great app!

This is by far the best app of its kind. UX is everything and they nail everything perfectly. It can be as simple as you need it, or as complex as you need it. Plenty of customizations to your liking, and it’s all done gorgeously, fun, and easy to use. Love it love it love it. Can’t rave enough about it.

Literally making me drink more water and workout more and do more healthy things because of how rewarding the colors and boxes are! I’m obsessed! I only just downloaded it, and I never write reviews for things, but this just deserved it. Also LOVE GitHub and coding and I can totally relate to the people who developed this app! Probably gonna purchase for life.

title.label: Great habit app after getting past initial confusion.

content.label:
Setting up a habit is confusing & unintuitive. This app looks very cool, but should be easier and more clear for new users to set up. Some sort of onboarding or tutorial would be helpful, perhaps even a throwaway habit should be pre-populated so it’s easier to see how to set one up.

Update: After the initial confusion, I’ve concluded that I really like this app. I’ve even paid for a year subscription. I’ve increased my rating from 3 to 4 stars.

title.label: Perfect middle between great design and intuitive simplicity

content.label: I tried several habit trackers before committing to HabitKit. It doesn’t gamify every little feature. It’s largely unopinionated in how you use it. The design is sleek and elegant and has just enough color to motivate your lizard brain to “fill more squares”. It’s gotten me more on track than any other app.

I really wish there were more widget sizes. The massive one doesn't fit on my main screen and it displays the name of the habit, not something I might want anyone peeping by to see. Love the aesthetic overall.

title.label: Streak is not a true streak

content.label: The streak is not a true streak, as it doesn’t reflect the number of consecutive days you’ve maintained the habit without interruption. It’s simply the total sum of all the days you’ve completed the habit, without counting whether they were continuous or not.

The simplicity and flexibility of this app is unmatched. After trying many other habit trackers, this is the first that I've been able to use consistently without wishing it worked differently!

A recent reviewer mentioned that the app had Apple Shortcuts integrations, which is a total game changer. I hope to create Strava, Oura, and Duolingo workflows in Shortcuts to automatically mark my habits as completed.

Thanks so much for this great app, Sebastian! 🙌
The interface is well made and the premium version is very reasonably priced. This app is not a complex task tracker and that is a good thing, it is light weight and does one thing well.

I went into this thinking that this would be the app of all apps, that it would solve all my habits issues, it doesn’t. I spent something like $30 to get it on my homepage for a year(stupid, right?), and it does what it’s supposed to, but not much more
I love the visuals on the app to help track habits. The widget is great as well. The developer is responsive and the features in the pipeline are prioritized

title.label: Great App for Stacking New Habits

content.label: Over the years I have tried numerous streak apps from the productivity category.  Most have a poor interface and/or leave much to be desired.  Habitkit breathes new life into what is normally a boring, mundane task.  The simple minimalist design is right on for my needs.  I used the app for about 6 weeks before purchasing the upgrade seems well worth the extra cost.  Unlocking a bit more features but not over-complicating it too much....I'm pleased with it and looking forward to staying on track.

I’ve tried a few habit apps, and absolutely love using this one so far. The user experience is extremely intuitive and easy to use, and has (almost) all the features I was looking for. Just as an example, the Shortcuts integration is great for me - I was able to integrate HabitKit into an existing Shortcut I was using for recording a daily journal, and so now recording one will also automatically mark the habit complete for the day too. The widgets are really nice too and improve the overall interaction.

All that said, there are just a few additional features I’d like to see. First, a MacOS version of the app would be great, though I can confirm that it does work to install the iOS version. However, it would really be awesome if it could sync to iCloud both to make this actually usable, as well as to make it easy when you get a new device. There is an export / import feature for this but this would make it a lot. Lee seamless. Finally, it would be nice to have additional Shortcuts support - the ability to look at past completions / streaks, change completion for other dates, export / import from Shortcut, etc.

With that list, why did I still give it 5 stars? Because even as-is it is incredibly useful and I would recommend it to everyone even without these features (though they would be great!)

I just recently started using this app because I like the UX and how it easily conveys how often you are doing something similar to GitHub. So far I really enjoy it and I am excited to keep tracking my habits 🤞🏽
One thing I wish there was is the ability to have a widget that can display multiple habits even if in a condensed list view or something similar. I would also like to see if there is any way to add the ability on making a habit to quit something (I.e create a habit and I want to make sure that I don’t do this habit more than x amount of times per week/month/day etc. or something similar. Basically if I stay under my set limit then the habit is considered complete or good)
Great app, love the visualization options! It’s so satisfying to see your streaks filling up that grid.

I’ve been through many habit trackers over the years and they never seem to stick or work for me. This is the first one that has been simple and intuitive to use and follow. This one just clicks for me. Definitely try it out.

I’ve tried many habit apps, and I think HabitKite simplistic approach is what keeps me using it. 

Many of the others (even Atoms from James Clear) is over complicated and almost… distracting. 

But with HabitKit I really just want to fill in the boxes. 

The UX is smooth, it’s easy to customize and really does “simple habit tracking” really well. 

I’ve also followed Sebastian’s journey for quite some time, and his ability to continue improving such a simple app and respond to users is something most indie apps lack. 

Can’t recommend this app enough.

title.label: This is what will get me completing New Years Resolutions

content.label:
I always struggled finding a good habit tracker app, because all the dedicated ones look bad, or their feature set was never that large. They’d just be glorified counter apps. 

So once I tried this one I was so filled with glee to see a beautiful dark mode, a git esque visualization with different views, great sorting, etc. 

Instantly went for the pro subscription cause I wanted to add habits for everything, highly recommend this one
Simple effective app with a pleasant design. I don’t use all the features, just track a few daily habits. I asked the developer a question via email and he was very kind in his reply.

I love an app that does exactly what it says on the tin. Works well with shortcuts for automation. Happy to purchase the lifetime pro license. Data seems local so works great no matter your network conditions and you never see a loading spinner 

Feature requests: 

- support CloudKit for syncing across devices. 
- Deep links for specific habits or filters
- add a simple small one click tracking widget. The current widgets should open the selected habit instead of the dashboard too 

If you find NFC tags fussy for habit tracking, flic buttons work alright if you have pushcut + an automation server (use the web request action to trigger your habit tracking shortcut). 

It’d be great if there was a way to support habit tracking actions in home automations (not just personal automations) to avoid this whole song and dance. 

Overall, great application, would recommend to a friend

title.label: Just what I was looking for!

content.label:
I tried a bunch of habit tracking apps, and all of them were too complicated in the ways that I didn’t want and not polished enough in the ways I needed. This app strikes the perfect balance, providing a simple and straightforward way to track daily habits.

The only thing I would improve is the notifications—the alert text is fairly generic and it would be more encouraging to be able to define custom messages instead.
Good app I can see you use flutter instead of Native I’m dev too I can contribute with us. Thanks

title.label: Really good, could be amazing - just a few small fixes

content.label:
Let’s be clear, if you want to gamify a habit in a very pretty way (Ala GitHub contributions), this is the best. But there are a few feature requests/suggestions that could make it better.

#1 - Basic iPad support. Does need to be a lot, but something that better fits landscape for iPad would be appreciated. 

#2 - Synchronization - You can run the app on iOS/macOS/iPad. But there is no way to sync. Especially as a pro feature, it’d be nice to have a built in sync. 

#3 - Watch app. Again - Something super simple as a way to tick off the tasks done would be really nice when doing those exercise type habits.

I paid for pro almost immediately after starting to use it. The dot grid is such a great way to get a feel for how good you’ve been about keeping up with your habit goals and then there’s all these detailed stats you get on top of that. The design of the app is great too, very easy to use and and simple enough that you aren’t distracted from the info you’re looking at. It’s worth the cost of the pro version for sure. It would be cool to get some new themes to play with and be able to set multiple reminders for habits that have multiple completions in a day but I’m sure the developer already has that in mind for future updates.

title.label: It Helps to Improve Your good habits

content.label: It is like GitHub of Habit
Simple but solid. Been looking for something that has everything I need but is simple at the same time. Worth the cost. I’m very glad there is a one time payment option.
iPad support please!
Too pricy for me, twice the cost of same subscription on android.

title.label: fantastic app for iphone. needs an ipad native version.

content.label:
HabitKit is a great app. The UI is very easy to understand and navigate. While pared down compared to other similar apps (Productive, Habitify, etc), it”s also quick and easy to set up new habits. Tracking and entering data is very fast and easy, which makes it much more likely that I’ll 1) use the app, 2)stay on track with habits I’m working to implement.

It definitely needs an iPad native app.
